title: sse-framing-partial-json-token-ordering-fix
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: clients using the OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoint observed occasional invalid/partial JSON payloads when multiple SSE events and token-level fragments were interleaved. Root cause was a race between the framing/delimiter insertion logic and the token event queue: delimiters (closing characters and event separators) could be emitted after subsequent token fragments, producing malformed partial JSON at the client. This PR fixes ordering and framing bugs and adds deterministic tests. Summary of changes: - Reworked SSE framer to treat delimiters (partial-json separators, event boundary markers) as first-class tokens with ordering guarantees; delimiters are now enqueued and drained in the same sequence as token events. - Introduced token-level sequence ids for in-flight fragments and added a small ordering window to ensure fragments are emitted in strict logical order even under backpressure. - Fixed a race where connection flush on stream close could reorder the final delimiter and trailing token fragments. - Updated OpenAI compatibility adapter to preserve token/event ordering semantics and removed a heuristic that attempted to coalesce delimiters late in the pipeline. - Added unit, integration, and fuzz tests that exercise partial-json delimiter ordering and token-event interleaving across a range of chunk sizes and concurrency patterns. - Improved logging for streaming diagnostics and added a short-run performance microbenchmark. Backports: backported the critical fix to the release/2026.02 branch in a follow-up hotfix PR (ENG-5580). Testing: ran unit + integration + e2e streaming tests and a fuzz suite against the streaming adapter with 10k randomized sequences. Results show the ordering failure rate dropped to 0/10k and latency impact is negligible (~0.4% median increase under heavy load). Rollout: merged to main and deployed to canary for dedicated and hosted API for 48h; no regressions observed. Notes: this PR intentionally avoids heavy refactors to minimize risk; the next follow-up will consider a consolidated streaming pipeline abstraction. Related: ENG-5523, SUP-2019. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] fuzz tests [x] send canary [x] update docs

Maya Singh: Please call out the expected latency impact in the PR description and confirm there's no regression for small-chunk fast paths.
